subject: Inference engine recommendations for Tremont — cost/latency tradeoffs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@tremont.ai>, Samir Joshi <samir.j@tremont.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Inference engine recommendations for Tremont — cost/latency tradeoffs

Hi Maria / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciated the walkthrough and the latency/cost constraints you shared. Per our conversation, I ran a quick synthesis of candidate inference engines that map to Tremont’s requirements (low 95th Pct latency on short-query path, half-million tokens/day expected, tight budget vs. quality tradeoffs). Below is a concise slate plus the immediate asks so we can validate in a focused eval sprint.

Recommended engine slate (high-level):
- Redwood-Edge-16Q (int8) — Best balance for your throughput profile. 95th Pct latency ~140ms at target concurrency in our sandbox; strong quality on code and analytics prompts; mid-tier cost.
- Falcon-40B-INT8 (optimized kernels) — Higher quality on long-form synthesis; 95th Pct ~220ms in our baseline; cheaper per-token than 16Q for large outputs when batched.
- LlamaX-7B-4bit (quantized) — Lowest cost and lowest latency (95th Pct ~95ms); slightly lower factuality for dense analytics prompts but often acceptable after prompt tuning.

Tradeoff notes (quick):
- If you prioritize sub-150ms P95 for single-turn queries, LlamaX-7B or Redwood-Edge in 16Q int8 are the only realistic picks without adding dedicated burst capacity.
- For multi-turn assistants or long-code generation, Falcon-40B gives better contextual coherence at cost of latency unless we use caching strategies.
- We can reduce per-token cost by ~20–35% with prefix/KV caching and model-specific prompt templates (I’ve attached a starter prompt pack).

Attached: tremont_benchmarks_v1.csv (baseline latency/cost across engines) and tremont_prompt_set_v1.zip (initial prompt variants we used). Also shared a Drive folder with raw perf logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_Tremont-eval

Immediate asks / proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the latency SLO target for single-turn queries (is 150ms P95 the hard cutoff or a goal)?
2) We propose a 5-day focused eval: Redwood will run targeted benchmarks using your top-10 prompts and 3 representative datasets from your team. Outcome: validated P95, per-token cost estimate, and a short quality report.
3) If that works, we’ll provision a short-lived dedicated slot to run canary tests (estimated 48–72 hours).

I’ve looped in Karthik and Marissa for scope + procurement cadence. If you’d like, we can include an itemized cost comparison with Dedicated vs Hosted for your projected throughput.

Best,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Alvarez <maria@tremont.ai>

Subject: Re: Inference engine recommendations for Tremont — cost/latency tradeoffs

Ben —

Thanks for the concise slate and the attachments — very helpful. Quick answers / clarifications from our side:
- Latency SLO: 150ms P95 is our target for lookups and short analytic queries (single-turn). For multi-step workflows we can accept up to 300ms P95.
- Budget: our finance team has a soft cap of ~$2.5k/mo initially while we validate (we can expand after PO).
- Quality: factual correctness on analytics prompts is non-negotiable — we need to avoid hallucinations on financial metrics.

Can you confirm whether Redwood-Edge-16Q requires Dedicated capacity to meet 140ms P95, or if that was on the Hosted sandbox? Also — curious what caching strategy you recommend for multi-turns (KV vs prefix).

Happy to proceed with the 5-day eval if you can align with the SLO and budget framing.

Thanks,
Maria
Head of Product
Tremont Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@tremont.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Inference engine recommendations for Tremont — cost/latency tradeoffs

Hi Maria — looping in quick answers and an ops plan.

Short answers: 
- Redwood-Edge-16Q (int8): the 140ms P95 call was observed on our Hosted sandbox with a small reserved slot; to guarantee ~140ms at production concurrency we recommend a light Dedicated reservation (or Hosted with burst guarantees). We’ll quantify in the eval.
- Caching: for Tremont’s workflows I recommend a two-layer approach: prefix templates for repeated instruction framing (low cost, simple) + KV caching for multi-turn state where the same vectors reappear (gives biggest latency wins on follow-on turns). We’ll instrument hit-rate metrics in the eval.

Ops plan for the 5-day eval:
Day 0 (prep): ingest your 10 prompts (we already have the zipped prompt set).
Day 1–2: run single-turn latency & throughput sweeps across LlamaX-7B-4bit, Redwood-Edge-16Q, Falcon-40B-INT8.
Day 3: run quality-focused runs (factuality/regression checks) using your analytics dataset.
Day 4: integrate prefix/KV caching to measure P95 improvements, and run cost-estimation harness.
Day 5: deliver a short report + recommended engine + rollout plan.

Deliverables: benchmark CSV, per-engine quality scorecard, cost model (hosted vs dedicated), quick runbook for canary deployment (JIRA:INFR-842).

Marissa — can you own the quality/regression checks and drop the skeleton of the scoring rubric (precision/recall for extraction, hallucination rate, answer-switch consistency)?

Ben — please confirm procurement window (Maria — are we ok to start with a short PO for the eval slot or do you prefer Redwood-hosted with trial credits?).

Thanks,
Karthik
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
